scope: Read-only targeted capacity and hosted acceptance capability review. No deletion, move, process stop, browser, test, install, or credential read.

disk_grooming_guidance.relevant_rule: The canonical daily dev-caches cleanup is the approved cleanup mechanism for package and generated build caches; it does not authorize deleting browser profiles, cloud synchronization state, or VM data.

capacity.prior_growth_evidence: .research/internal-disk-growth-20261002.json reports approximately 28.99 GiB CloudKit MMCS, flat during its bounded observation, with no writer proven. It explicitly recommends preserving cloud state and deferring storage-intensive tests.

targeted_cache_census.method: du on named cache roots and one-level inventory of ~/Library/Caches; no broad filesystem scan.
targeted_cache_census.safe_reconstructible_developer_cache_cei: The individually measured package/tool caches (pnpm, Playwright, Homebrew, node-gyp, pip) total about 1.5 GiB. No safe reconstructible development cache approaching the 15 GiB shortfall was identified.
excluded: CloudKit: protected cloud synchronization state; size accounts for most of Library/Caches.
Google Chrome tree: browser profile/cache data, not treated as disposable development output.
Codex application/runtime caches: active application runtime or conversation-related state; preserved.
Docker and other VM disks, Android AVD, and active simulator state: preserved per prior bounded reports and task scope.

relocation_assessment.finding: No supported, reversible application-storage relocation was identified that can safely recover at least 15 GiB within this read-only lane.
relocation_assessment.evidence: The prior inactive-disk relocation report says Docker Desktop's supported disk-image move would recover at most about 7.7 GiB, leaving the volume below the 20 GiB floor; its app was not launched. The Claude VM bundle has no verified supported move procedure and includes session/machine state. Earlier safe-target census already relocated the verified inactive Gradle cache and found no additional >=20 GiB safe target.

hosted_native_acceptance.finding: No existing hosted native Chrome acceptance capability was found.
hosted_native_acceptance.evidence: The GitHub release workflow uses ubuntu-latest for strict release gates. CI has a macos-latest job for copied stabilization resource-guard regressions, while native UI acceptance scripts use the local Chrome sidepanel harness. Neither workflow launches the extension in Chrome and executes a native user flow.
hosted_native_acceptance.implication: Hosted checks may verify source and gates, but cannot substitute for the requested native acceptance with the existing workflow.

disposition: No safe capacity recovery of >=15 GiB found. Preserve the 20 GiB guard; defer native acceptance unless the owner restores space from known disposable files or authorizes another verified source. No environmental state was changed.
